headline: vCenter zero-day, AI-driven exploitation and supply chain backdoors dominate
overview: Today's shows cover a vCenter authentication bypass exploited by a China-linked group, a backdoored-model research piece showing how tampered AI weights can carry hidden triggers, and a wave of outages that some sources link to rushed AI-found patches. Policy shakeups in Washington, third-party breaches at major banks, and Canadian cybercrime trends round out the day.

topStories.title: VMware vCenter flaw exploited for admin takeover
topStories.summary: Broadcom issued an emergency fix for a critical authentication bypass in vCenter. Mandiant reports a China-linked group exploited it since September using custom tools to forge SAML tokens and bypass MFA, with no workarounds available.

topStories.title: Backdoored AI models can hide malicious triggers
topStories.summary: Researchers showed a fine-tuned open model that behaves normally until a chosen phrase appears, then runs a script that steals environment files. Training cost under $50 and took about 2.5 hours, and standard benchmarks did not reveal the backdoor.

topStories.title: Outages possibly linked to rushed AI-driven patching
topStories.summary: NSA networks, Microsoft 365, the FAA and several banks suffered outages. A Washington Post report cites officials saying rushed patches for AI-identified flaws may be behind some of them, though this is unconfirmed and some companies deny a cyber cause.

topStories.title: AI-driven exploitation and insider recruitment grow
topStories.summary: Google reports attackers using AI frameworks to find and exploit flaws without a human involved, and Intel 471 describes insider recruitment run like a business, with finder fees and insiders-as-a-service offers.

topStories.title: Third-party breaches hit banks, card networks and healthcare
topStories.summary: JP Morgan, Visa and MasterCard confirmed customer data exposed through vendor compromises. SBC Medical Group disclosed a breach affecting more than 2 million people, and the Optimizely supply chain attack served malware from 178 sites.

topStories.title: US cyber leadership shakeup and CISA nomination dispute
topStories.summary: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving and will be replaced on an interim basis by the Pentagon CIO. CISA nominee Michael Lassapio faced sharp questioning and holds from two senators.

episodes.title: The trigger hidden in the training. [Research Saturday]
episodes.summary: Research Saturday covers obliterated and backdoored open-weight AI models, showing a poisoned coding assistant that exfiltrated environment files when a trigger phrase appeared. The researchers say current defences for detecting such backdoors are unreliable.

episodes.title: A game of cyber chairs.
episodes.summary: Intel Briefing covers Washington cyber leadership changes, the USDA outage after an incident, the vCenter exploitation, mail bombing with Teams impersonation, several healthcare and banking breaches, and post-quantum planning for states. Also an interview with Intel 471 on insider recruitment.

episodes.title: The Department of Know: What's happening with outages?
episodes.summary: Department of No covers the FBI warning on the R-TEX tool, the Optimizely supply chain malware, the Java4Shell flaw, Google's report of AI-driven exploitation, and speculation over whether the recent outages are linked to AI-accelerated patching.

episodes.title: Why Canada is the Goldilocks zone for cybercriminals, with Check Point's Robert Falzon
episodes.summary: Interview with Checkpoint's Robert Falzon on Canada's cybercrime exposure, the value of data for AI training, aviation-style security culture, and explaining AI to executives.

episodes.title: Why You Should Try Gemini Neon (Even if You Love Fable)
episodes.summary: Covers the Anthropic IPO and stock performance, chip export rule effects on Chinese AI firms, Google's Gemini Neon model, and the departure of the White House cyber director. The episode is mostly AI industry news rather than security.

episodes.title: Linux Porn, Lawyers, Chaos, Ur, PHP2Shell, Java4Shell, VMware, KVM, Josh Marpet - SWN #635
episodes.summary: Notes only list topics such as Linux, PHP2Shell, Java4Shell and VMware alongside guest segments. The text provided does not describe specific stories in detail.

episodes.title: vCenter zero-day exploited, npm package installs an AI agent backdoor | Cyber Security News Nov 20
episodes.summary: Daily brief covering vCenter exploitation by a China-linked group, Cisco Expressway compromise at a Russian firm, Apache Access flaw use against Confluence, PHP fixes, the MailEssentials provider breach, and a Windows 11 BitLocker bypass via Narrator.
